protagonist: A 58-year-old night-shift hospital cleaner keeps a notebook of the things patients say when they think no one is listening.
situation: A new administrator begins shredding the ward logs she has been quietly rescuing from the recycling for years.
conflict: The logs record a death her own family was told never happened, and the only copy is in a bag under her sink.
setting: A mid-sized city hospital and the estate on its edge, present day.
stakes: The only surviving account of what happened that night, and the job that pays for her mother's care.

protagonist: A 19-year-old hotel switchboard operator is the first in her family to reach university and works every weekend to stay there.
situation: An off-season guest reports a brother missing, and the guest's account of the week does not match the hotel's records.
conflict: Her supervisor wants the call log deleted before the police are called, and the log is the only proof the brother existed.
setting: A shuttered coastal resort town in late autumn, present day.
stakes: Her scholarship, her job, and a stranger who has no one else taking him seriously.

protagonist: A 41-year-old obituary translator for a regional newspaper lives with a father who no longer recognises her.
situation: The paper is bought by a group that wants flattering profiles of living donors instead of the dead.
conflict: Compliance keeps her father at home; refusal ends the only income that pays for his care.
setting: A shrinking industrial town on a river, present day.
stakes: Her father's remaining years at home, and the last thing she is good at.

protagonist: A 67-year-old retired bus driver has rented the same flat for forty years and knows every neighbour by the sound of their door.
situation: The building is sold, and the developer offers him a unit in the replacement tower on condition that he leaves quietly.
conflict: Accepting saves him and helps empty the building of the people who cannot afford the tower.
setting: A port city mid-redevelopment, present day.
stakes: The neighbours' homes, and the version of himself he has been able to live with.

protagonist: A 29-year-old veterinary technician, six months divorced, agrees to share custody of the dog with her ex-husband's new partner.
situation: The dog is diagnosed with a condition that gives it a year, and the shared calendar becomes the only structure either of them has.
conflict: They are falling for each other while the animal that brought them together is dying.
setting: A small mountain town with one vet practice, present day.
stakes: The friendship that makes the dog's last year bearable, and the ex-husband's forgiveness.

protagonist: A 35-year-old wedding photographer has never had a relationship longer than four months and photographs other people's vows for a living.
situation: A widower hires her to photograph a memorial garden through four seasons, one visit a month.
conflict: He is still married to a memory, and she is falling for a man who keeps asking her to document what he cannot let go of.
setting: Coastal California, present day.
stakes: Her professional reputation, his grief, and the first risk she has taken in years.

protagonist: A 44-year-old baker inherits a failing shop from the rival who put her out of business ten years earlier.
situation: The rival's son co-owns the building, wants to sell, and has no idea the recipes are hers.
conflict: Neither can afford to buy the other out, and the shop only works if they run it together.
setting: A northern English town, present day.
stakes: The shop, her name on the sign, and a decade of grudge she has organised her life around.

protagonist: A 26-year-old sign-language interpreter is assigned to a deaf comedian's farewell tour.
situation: Twelve cities, six weeks, and a performer who is losing his sight as well as his hearing.
conflict: Her professional code forbids the relationship, and the tour is his last chance to be seen on his own terms.
setting: A twelve-city club circuit, present day.
stakes: Her certification, his farewell, and the two people who understand the material.

protagonist: A 52-year-old insurance assessor has spent twenty years deciding which claims are honest.
situation: Three unrelated house fires in three towns share a damage pattern that only appears when a fire is set to hide something.
conflict: The common thread is her employer's largest client, and the file that would prove it is the one she signed off on.
setting: A drought-prone inland region over one summer, present day.
stakes: Her career, and the next house on the pattern.

protagonist: A 17-year-old finds a cassette in the pocket of a charity-shop coat and plays it on her grandfather's machine.
situation: The voice on the tape describes a burglary at her own address, in detail, in the past tense.
conflict: The burglary has not happened yet, and the police will not take a teenager seriously.
setting: A commuter town with one bus an hour, present day.
stakes: Her family's safety, and her grandfather, who owns the coat.

protagonist: A 38-year-old museum registrar catalogues a collection donated by the museum's largest funder.
situation: One object's paperwork predates the donor's birth, and the export licence carries a name that appears nowhere else.
conflict: The donor's money is keeping three departments open, and the object is almost certainly stolen.
setting: A provincial museum in a capital city, present day.
stakes: The collection, her job, and a family still waiting for the object to come home.

protagonist: A 61-year-old retired ferry captain kept a private log of every crossing and every passenger for thirty years.
situation: A man's alibi depends on a crossing the captain knows was cancelled for weather.
conflict: The log proves the alibi false, and the man's son is the officer asking.
setting: An island route off the Scottish coast, 1990s.
stakes: A murder charge, a career, and thirty years of a habit that was never meant to be evidence.

protagonist: A 33-year-old air-traffic controller spots a flight plan filed under a licence belonging to a colleague who died last year.
situation: The plan is legal, the aircraft is registered to a shell company, and the departure slot is in nine hours.
conflict: Reporting it brings her family under surveillance by people who know her shift pattern.
setting: A regional airport and the industrial belt around it, present day.
stakes: Her children's safety, her licence, and whatever the flight is carrying.

protagonist: A 45-year-old court stenographer has typed every word of the county's trials for eighteen years.
situation: She recognises a transcript she produced: two sentences have been changed, and the change convicts the defendant.
conflict: Her signature is on the certified record, and the man who altered it knows what she did ten years ago.
setting: A county courthouse in a mid-sized American city, present day.
stakes: An innocent man's sentence, her liberty, and the machine she is the only witness to.

protagonist: A 28-year-old logistics coordinator runs humanitarian cargo through a port controlled by three armed factions.
situation: One container of medicine is held at the dock, and all three factions have paid for it.
conflict: Whoever she releases it to will use the shortage against the other two, and the patients are in all three districts.
setting: A blockaded port city, present day.
stakes: Nine hundred patients, her neutrality, and the convoy that has to leave at dawn.

protagonist: A 50-year-old retired bomb-disposal officer now trains search dogs and trusts them more than people.
situation: His own dog alerts on a package at his daughter's school, on a day the school is running a lockdown drill.
conflict: The alert is either a hoax aimed at him or the real thing, and clearing the building means admitting publicly what he did in the war.
setting: A suburban town outside a military base, present day.
stakes: Four hundred children, his daughter's opinion of him, and the one call only he can make.

protagonist: A 39-year-old orbital debris auditor is paid to decide which pieces of junk are worth tracking.
situation: A fragment's trajectory implies a launch that no agency logged and a payload that never came down.
conflict: The fragment is on a decay path toward a crewed station, and the audit that would flag it is the one her employer buried.
setting: A commercial tracking station and low orbit, near future.
stakes: Six crew, her clearance, and the difference between debris and a weapon.

protagonist: A 22-year-old archivist on a generation ship is responsible for deleting files to keep the ship's storage under capacity.
situation: One file deletes itself when she opens it and leaves a note addressed to her by name.
conflict: The note describes a fault in the life-support schedule that the ship's council has voted not to record.
setting: A generation ship eleven years into its voyage, no planet in sight.
stakes: The archive, her position, and whether the next cohort is told the truth about the air.

protagonist: A 60-year-old soil scientist is on the last survey team before a planet is opened for settlement.
situation: The samples show a biosphere that has been engineered, and the engineering is younger than the planet.
conflict: Reporting it cancels the settlement contract that funds the survey, and someone has already begun clearing ground.
setting: A surveyed planet with one landing field, near future.
stakes: The planet's existing ecology, three thousand settlers in transit, and her own name on the clearance.

protagonist: A 31-year-old court interpreter is the only human certified for the first treaty negotiation with a non-human species.
situation: The species' language has no word for promise, and the treaty is built on one.
conflict: The delegation wants the nearest word translated as promise, and she knows the nearest word means something closer to debt.
setting: A neutral station above a shared moon, far future.
stakes: The treaty, two species' trust in translation, and her certification.

protagonist: A 24-year-old mapmaker's apprentice has spent six years copying coastlines that never move.
situation: Her maps begin to change overnight, but only on the copies she keeps for herself.
conflict: The guild burns inaccurate maps, and the changes are showing a road that does not exist yet.
setting: A harbour city and the surveys of its hinterland, pre-industrial.
stakes: Her apprenticeship, the guild's charter, and the town the road is heading for.

protagonist: A 47-year-old debt collector for a temple that lends years instead of money has never defaulted a client.
situation: Her own account is called in early, and the temple will not say who authorised it.
conflict: Collecting what she owes means taking years from the only person who ever forgave her.
setting: A river city of counting-houses and shrines, pre-industrial.
stakes: Her remaining years, her daughter's future, and the ledger she has trusted her whole life.

protagonist: A 16-year-old beekeeper tends the hives that mark the valley's border and keep the passes closed.
situation: The queen of the oldest hive stops laying, and the bees begin drifting into the next valley.
conflict: The village elders want the hive burned, and the drift is the only sign of where her missing brother went.
setting: A mountain valley with one road and one season, pre-industrial.
stakes: The border, the harvest, and the last trace of her brother.

protagonist: A 55-year-old executioner is the only person who can hear the last thoughts of the condemned.
situation: The next prisoner's thoughts are in a language no living person speaks, and they are addressed to him.
conflict: He must carry out the sentence before he understands what the prisoner is confessing.
setting: A walled capital with one gallows and a long list, pre-industrial.
stakes: The prisoner's soul, his own, and the kingdom's belief in what he does.

protagonist: A 34-year-old night auditor works alone at a hotel that is never full.
situation: The same guest checks in every night under a different name and always takes the same room.
conflict: The guest has begun checking in under her name, and the register shows her signature.
setting: A business hotel on an empty ring road, present day.
stakes: Her identity, her shift, and the room she has to clean in the morning.

protagonist: A 12-year-old is being bullied and has started eating lunch in the school boiler room.
situation: A door in the boiler room opens into a copy of the school, one day behind.
conflict: Everything she does there happens again tomorrow, and the people in it have started noticing her.
setting: A comprehensive school in a small town, present day.
stakes: Tomorrow, and the girl who will be blamed for what she does in it.

protagonist: A 43-year-old hospice nurse has sat with more than two hundred dying people.
situation: Her last four patients have described the same waiting room, down to the colour of the chairs.
conflict: The fifth patient is her mother, and she has started describing it too.
setting: A hospice on the edge of a moor, present day.
stakes: Her mother's last weeks, her own belief that she is a good nurse, and what is in the room.

protagonist: A 29-year-old sound engineer restores a 1970s recording for a private archive.
situation: Under the music there is a voice describing the room she is working in, in the present tense.
conflict: The voice is getting closer to her chair, and the archive wants the original returned by Friday.
setting: A converted studio in a warehouse district, present day.
stakes: Her hearing, her contract, and the thing the tape is counting down to.

protagonist: A 30-year-old widow runs her husband's printing press in a city where unlicensed presses are smashed.
situation: A customer orders a pamphlet that names the men who ordered the last press destroyed.
conflict: The job pays for her children's winter, and the customer is the man who signed her husband's warrant.
setting: A European printing city, 1580s.
stakes: The press, her children, and the record of what happened to her husband.

protagonist: A 19-year-old telephone operator works the exchange during a strike she voted for.
situation: The company keeps the exchange open with strike-breakers, and she is the only one who knows which lines the union is using.
conflict: Every call she connects is evidence against her own side, and the police are asking her to remember them.
setting: A manufacturing city during a general strike, 1919.
stakes: The strike, her family's rent, and a friend who will be arrested tonight.

protagonist: A 40-year-old midwife in a rural parish has attended every birth in three villages for twenty years.
situation: A magistrate requires her to testify about a birth she attended in a house where the child later disappeared.
conflict: The truth protects the mother and destroys the family that has fed her through every winter.
setting: An agricultural parish, 1790s.
stakes: A mother's life, the midwife's licence to practise, and the village's trust.

protagonist: A 26-year-old lighthouse keeper's daughter runs the light while her father is ill.
situation: The occupying force orders the light kept on for its convoys, and the resistance uses the dark.
conflict: Every night she chooses which ships to save, and both sides know the light is hers.
setting: An occupied coast, 1943.
stakes: Her father's life, the crews on both sides, and the village below the light.

protagonist: A 36-year-old cave surveyor maps systems that flood every spring and has never lost a team member.
situation: Her team is two days from the entrance when the rain arrives early and the only exit is a passage she has not finished surveying.
conflict: The unfinished passage may dead-end, and the injured member cannot survive the long route.
setting: A limestone cave system in a monsoon region, present day.
stakes: Four lives, her record, and the survey that justifies the expedition.

protagonist: A 58-year-old skipper delivers other people's yachts across oceans and has stopped asking why.
situation: He takes a three-week crossing with three strangers and a radio that only receives.
conflict: The owner's instructions and the weather router disagree, and one of the crew is not who the paperwork says.
setting: The North Atlantic, present day.
stakes: The boat, the four of them, and the delivery fee that is his pension.

protagonist: A 21-year-old wildfire lookout spends five months alone on a ridge with a radio and a compass.
situation: She spots a fire behind her position, between her and the only trail down.
conflict: Calling it in brings the crew up the trail, and the wind is turning toward the ridge.
setting: A forested ridge in a dry summer, present day.
stakes: Her crew, the valley below, and the one decision she has trained for.

protagonist: A 40-year-old river guide leads a trip whose permit expired two days ago and knows the fine falls on her.
situation: Her client has lied about his experience, and the river is running two grades above the booking.
conflict: Turning back means the fine; continuing means the client's life in her hands on water he cannot read.
setting: A mountain river with one put-in, present day.
stakes: Her licence, the client, and the two porters who will not leave her.

protagonist: A 30-year-old assistant to a minor celebrity handles the diary, the luggage and the apologies.
situation: A booking error sends her employer to open a regional produce awards instead of a film premiere.
conflict: The audience has no idea who he is, the compère is his ex-wife, and the trophy has already been engraved.
setting: A hotel conference suite in a market town, present day.
stakes: Her job, his dignity, and a crate of prize marrows.

protagonist: A 48-year-old wedding officiant was ordained online and has just discovered the denomination requires quarterly reports.
situation: The reports ask for details of ceremonies he performed from memory in a field.
conflict: Filing honestly dissolves the denomination; filing badly means an audit of every wedding he has done.
setting: A rural county with one registry office, present day.
stakes: Four hundred marriages, his licence, and a couple whose wedding was in a barn.

protagonist: A 25-year-old cheese roller has won his local hill four years running and is now sponsored.
situation: The sponsor's contract pays a bonus if he places second, because the footage is better.
conflict: His whole identity is winning, and the sponsor owns the hill's insurance.
setting: A steep English hill with a cheese and a crowd, present day.
stakes: His record, his sponsor's money, and the twelve-year-old who is faster than him.

protagonist: A 52-year-old neighbourhood watch coordinator takes the role extremely seriously and has a lanyard.
situation: A film crew shooting in the street at night looks exactly like a burglary ring to a man with a clipboard.
conflict: His intervention makes the local news, and the production company wants him in the film.
setting: A suburban street with one parking space, present day.
stakes: His reputation, the crew's shoot, and the truth about the man he tackled.
